qs.q: A patient presents with symptoms of GERD. In mild cases of reflux oesophagitis, what is the predominant endoscopic and histological appearance of the distal esophageal mucosa?
o: Marked basal zone hypoplasia and absent lamina propria papillae
Extensive mucosal necrosis with fungal hyphae invasion
Simple hyperaemia with often unremarkable mucosal histology
qs.e: In mild GERD, the only alteration may be simple hyperaemia (redness on endoscopy), and mucosal histology is often unremarkable. Histological hallmarks like basal zone hyperplasia appear in more significant, severe disease.
